body.name: Imagination Studio 4.3.1
body.body:
Imagination Studio 4.3.1 runs on **one to four local NVIDIA GPUs** on one Linux machine, and raises a Mac's default install to **96 GB**. The engines are the same as 4.2.1's.

## New

- **Local NVIDIA GPU workers** (#177, akol1's #168 carried onto 4.3.0, thank you @akol1).
  - On a workstation with up to four NVIDIA cards, the Studio runs on one card and starts a worker on each other compute card.
  - **Machine → Sparks** shows each card's VRAM, utilization and job.
  - **Card pinning:** workers are pinned by card UUID, so a card whose order changed is caught rather than used by mistake.
  - **Shared RAM:** jobs wait their turn for the machine's RAM. A job that can never fit is refused at once, and the refusal names what holds the memory.
  - **Which card the Studio uses:** with two or more compute cards, set `STUDIO_GPU` to the Studio's own card; the launch script asks for it. A display card is only used when you say so.
  - **Limit:** a fifth card is refused.
  - See [Local GPUs](https://github.com/drowzeys/Imagination-Studio-by-keys-Wasserman/blob/v4.3.1/docs/rtx-pro-6000.md#one-to-four-local-gpus).

## Changed

- **A Mac needs 96 GB for the default install** (video, voice, music, Bolt), up from 64 GB (#178).
  - **Pictures only:** `bash oneshot-setup.sh --image-only` still needs 48 GB. A fresh install on a smaller Mac stops before downloading anything and offers it.
  - **Upgrading a 64 to 95 GB Mac:** `--upgrade` keeps what's installed, updates it to this version without fetching weights, and says the new minimum. Video keeps running there; the Voice and Music tabs now say they need 96 GB.
  - **Unchanged:** the 128 GB (MiniMax H3 Turbo, Ref2VA) and 192 GB (Upscale, Remove a person) tiers.

## Install or update

- **Update:** `git pull`, then run `--upgrade` as usual and restart the app. Installed engines whose commit didn't change are kept.
- **Prebuilt parts:** unchanged. The carrier image stays `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:4.2.1`, and the Mac Bolt archive stays the v4.2.1 asset.

## Tested

- **CI** on #177, #178 and this release.
- **#177 on a DGX Spark:**
  - The full suite: 1,359 passed, 0 failed.
  - Simulated cards:
    - a display card plus a compute card, in either order;
    - two compute cards with and without `STUDIO_GPU`;
    - four cards, plus a refused fifth;
    - every shutdown left nothing behind.
  - RAM admission against real memory.
  - A real 30 s song rendered from the branch.
  - **Not tested by us:** two physical cards rendering at once. akol1 reports a two-card run.
- **#178 on Linux and a Mac:** new installer tests fake a Mac at 32 to 128 GB, plus the Voice and Music refusals at 64 and 95 GB.

body.name: Imagination Studio 4.3.0
body.body:
Imagination Studio 4.3.0 adds **Apps**, every tool of the Studio as a one-click app. Songs can now be cleared to the trash, and the Library's automatic captions no longer load a Bolt that can't see. The engines are the same as 4.2.1's.

## New

- **Apps** (#176, Sam Wasserman): a new room at the top of the sidebar.
  - **Nine kinds** (Cinema, Characters, Camera, Effects, Styles, Sound, Finish, Filmmaker Suite and Studio), with a search box. A DGX Spark lists 61 apps.
  - **Pre-filled forms:** each app opens the Studio's own form with its model, LoRA or start already chosen. It adds no new engine or server route.
  - **Nothing to set up first:**
    - A LoRA that isn't installed yet opens Looks on that LoRA.
    - A Library action (Character Swap, Restyle, Fix, Extend, Remove a person, Upscale, Captions, Turnaround) first asks for a clip or picture from your newest takes.
    - An app this machine can't run says why on its card.
  - **Character Swap · Openjutsu:** the swap is named for what it is, Comfy Org's Openjutsu made inside the Studio, fully local. Search for Openjutsu or Genjutsu to find it.
  - **Shortcuts and phones:** every app is in ⌘K. On a phone, Apps sits in the More sheet.
  - **Marks and art:** YuE2's mark appears beside its name in Music and in Apps; it's recorded in THIRD-PARTY-MARKS.md. There's new key art for Captions, Titles, Restyle, Fix and Extend.

## Fixed

- **Songs can be cleared to the trash** (#170, Sam Wasserman).
  - **What goes with it:** a cleared song takes its record, and for a YuE2 song its score folder, to the trash. *Put back* restores every file.
  - **What stays:** a song stays where it is while a film's soundtrack or a queued export or finish names it, or while it's still being made. The skipped list says why.
  - **Before:** a finished song could never be cleared.
  - **Test fix:** a test that counted other jobs' engine unloads no longer fails in some full runs.
- **Library captions don't load a Bolt with no vision** (#175). A Mac's Metal Bolt reads text only. The automatic clip captions used to load it for every new clip, get no answer, and keep it from unloading. Now the captioner skips a Bolt without a vision tower, and the Studio's Bolt unloads on its usual idle timer.
  - If you turned off Settings → "Describe new clips automatically" on a Mac because of this, you can turn it back on.

## Install or update

- **Update:** `git pull`, then reload the page; the 4.2.1 engines are unchanged.
  - On a DGX Spark or a Linux workstation, `--upgrade` is still safe to run: `bash oneshot-setup-spark.sh --upgrade` or `oneshot-setup-rtx-6000.sh --upgrade`. It keeps every installed engine whose commit didn't change.
  - Restart the app after either.
- **New install:** clone the repo and run `bash oneshot-setup.sh`.
- **Prebuilt parts:** unchanged. The carrier image stays `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:4.2.1`, and the Mac Bolt archive stays the v4.2.1 asset.

## Tested

- CI on each pull request and on `main`.
- New `tests/test_apps_page.py`: rooms, kinds, LoRA use, install and unsupported cases, the take picker for Library actions, search and ⌘K.
- New `tests/test_clear.py` cases for songs.
- On a DGX Spark: 61 of 61 apps ready; LoRA apps open Create with the look on; Upscale lists recent clips; the phone layout at 375 px has no sideways scroll.

body.name: Imagination Studio 4.2.1
body.body:
Imagination Studio 4.2.1 removes build-machine paths from the prebuilt engines. The engines' code and output are unchanged.

## What changed

- **Engines:** the H3 engine (`libtf_h3.so`) and Drama 3's `drama3-generate` and `libtensorfold_drama3.so` for the DGX Spark carried build folders in their debug sections, unchanged since 3.3.0. So did the Mac's Bolt `tensorfold-native` in 4.2.0. All four are now stripped of debug information. Their code, data and CUDA kernels are byte for byte the same; only a few header bytes differ.
- **Carrier:** `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:4.2.1` holds the stripped H3 and Drama 3. The Mac Bolt archive on this release is the stripped one.
- **Guard:** `scripts/build-carrier.sh` now strips every engine it packs and refuses a payload that names the building machine's home folder or user. A new test checks this.

## Same output

Old and new builds were run alternately (old, new, new, old) on the same machine and seeds:

| Engine | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| H3 (DGX Spark) | 5 s at 864×480, FastH3 8 steps, seed 7 | video and audio byte-identical in all 4 runs; about 118 s both ways |
| Drama 3 (DGX Spark) | 3 lines, seed 7 | WAVs byte-identical in all 4 runs |
| Bolt (Mac) | 7 greedy prompts | 7 of 7 identical replies |

## Update

`git pull`, then `--upgrade` as usual, and restart the app. An installed engine is kept while its commit is unchanged. To take the stripped builds, remove only each engine's version marker before `--upgrade`: on a DGX Spark `rm $PREFIX/tf-h3/commit $PREFIX/drama3/commit $PREFIX/drama3/BUILD`, then run `bash scripts/setup-voice.sh` (or `oneshot-setup-spark.sh --voice`) for Drama 3. On a Mac, `rm $PREFIX/bolt-metal/COMMIT`. Don't delete the `drama3` folder: it also holds the converted codec link, `codec-v1.safetensors`. If it was deleted, `setup-voice.sh` converts the codec again in a few seconds.

body.name: Imagination Studio 4.2.0
body.body:
Imagination Studio 4.2.0 moves the engines built on TensorFold from **1.1.5** to **1.1.8**, the latest release, with the same output. It ships new prebuilt parts with them.

## Install or update

- **New install:** clone the repo and run `bash oneshot-setup.sh`.
- **Update:** `git pull`, then on Linux `bash oneshot-setup-spark.sh --upgrade` (or `oneshot-setup-rtx-6000.sh --upgrade`), or on a Mac `bash oneshot-setup.sh --upgrade`. Then restart the app. The engine each one replaces stays beside it (`bolt.previous`).
- **Prebuilt parts:**
  - the carrier `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:4.2.0`;
  - the Bolt archives below, for CUDA (DGX Spark) and Metal (Mac). Their checksums are pinned in the installer.

## Engines

| Engine | TensorFold | Output vs 1.1.5 | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, DGX Spark (`bolt-lilicorr-118`) | 1.1.8 | identical replies, 7 of 7 prompts in 3 alternating runs | first token 62–84 ms (was 64–102), 74–82 tok/s (was 73–76) |
| Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, Mac (`bolt-metal-118`) | 1.1.8 | identical replies, 7 of 7 | first token 119 ms (was 126), 134 tok/s |
| MiniMax Music 3, DGX Spark and Mac | 1.1.8 | byte-identical songs for the same seed | unchanged (57–58 s on a Spark, 23.2 s on a Mac) |
| YuE2 decode engine | stays on 1.1.5 | its GPU test passes on 1.1.8; a whole song wasn't timed | — |
| Drama 3 (DGX Spark), H3 / FastH3 | unchanged | — | — |

## Fixes

- **Zig is checked before it is unpacked in every build.** The CUDA builds of Bolt, H3, Music 3 and Drama 3 now share `spark/zig.sh`, which checks the archive against ziglang.org's published SHA-256. The Mac's Music 3 build gets the published sum; before, it had none.
- **No machine paths in the engines.** The binaries contain no home-folder path, and the archives are packed owner 0/0.
- **Includes 4.1.2:**
  - several NVIDIA cards without `STUDIO_GPU`;
  - scripts' refusals in their own words;
  - Qwen optional beside FLUX3-K.

## Tested

- Full suite on a DGX Spark, plus CI.
- Fresh installs take Bolt from the release archive and from the new carrier, and take Music 3, H3 and Drama 3 from the carrier. A tampered archive is refused.
- studio-check: the API tier passed 12 of 12, plus the local-brain and 10 s music checks.
- The Mac: Bolt and Music 3 A/B against the 1.1.5 builds.

Credits: TensorFold (Ash Hart) 1.1.8; NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt; MiniMax Music 3; Zig.

body.name: Imagination Studio 4.1.2
body.body:
Imagination Studio 4.1.2 fixes installs on machines with two or more NVIDIA cards, and makes Qwen optional on a machine that has FLUX3-K.

## Install or update

- **New install:** clone the repo and run `bash oneshot-setup.sh`.
- **Update:** `git pull`, then `bash oneshot-setup-spark.sh --upgrade` (or `oneshot-setup-rtx-6000.sh --upgrade`) on Linux, then restart the app. A Mac only needs the pull and a restart.
- **Prebuilt parts are unchanged:** the carrier image stays `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:3.3.0` and the Spark's Bolt engine stays the v3.3.3 asset.

## What's fixed

- **Two or more NVIDIA cards and no `STUDIO_GPU` (#169).** Every installer entry now chooses the card the way the app's start script does.
  - A single compute card is used even at index 0 beside a display card. A workstation with a small display card listed first no longer installs against it, or refuses video because "this one has 8 GB".
  - With two compute cards, the installer stops and asks for `STUDIO_GPU`.
  - The memory guard reads the same card when the server is started on its own.
- **A script that says why it stopped is reported in its own words (#169).** It no longer gets " (status 1)" after it; the status is kept only when the script printed nothing.
- **Qwen is optional beside FLUX3-K (#171).**
  - `--verify` and `--upgrade` say Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo is not installed, and that it's optional, instead of stopping at "✗ missing".
  - They no longer print a ✓ for files they just called missing.
  - studio-check marks the Qwen edit and angle checks as not applicable.

## Tested

- Full suite on a DGX Spark, plus CI.
- Multi-GPU cases on a Spark with a simulated `nvidia-smi`:
  - a display card at index 0 with an RTX Pro 6000 at index 1;
  - two compute cards;
  - `STUDIO_GPU=1`.
- Not tested on real multi-card x86 machines.

body.name: 4.1.1: YuE2 songs, Character Swap and an honest Director on a DGX Spark, Mac Studio, RTX Pro 6000 and RTX 5090
body.body:
Imagination Studio 4.1.1 brings together 3.4.0 (**YuE2** songs and **Character Swap**, by Sam Wasserman), 4.1.0 (an **honest Director**: a run report that counts outcomes, failed takes kept in the Library, shots that keep their cast, also by Sam) and the fixes from review and testing on a DGX Spark, a Mac Studio, a simulated RTX Pro 6000 (96 GB) and a simulated RTX 5090 (32 GB).

## Install or update

- **New install:** clone the repo and run `bash oneshot-setup.sh`. On Linux it hands off to the CUDA installer, so `--yue2` and `--swap` work there too.
- **Update:** `git pull`, then `bash oneshot-setup-spark.sh --upgrade` (or `oneshot-setup-rtx-6000.sh --upgrade`) on Linux, then restart the app. A Mac only needs the pull and a restart. `--swap` installs now fetch the int8 Ref2VA (21 GB) it runs on, not the 40 GB bf16 file.
- **Prebuilt parts are unchanged:** the carrier image stays `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:3.3.0` and the Spark's Bolt engine is the v3.3.3 asset. None of their pinned commits changed, so the installer keeps fetching them as before. The YuE2 engine builds from source in about a minute, and Zig's archive is checked against ziglang.org's SHA-256.

## What's new

See README "New in 4.1.1", "New in 4.1.0" and "New in 3.4.0". The 4.1.1 fixes:
- **Character Swap checks memory before it is queued.** The peaks were measured per machine (see the table below). A 32 GB card without `STUDIO_ROOM_MB` is refused with the card's name and the setting to change.
- **A part with nobody in it is refused in words.** A swap needs SAM 3.1 to be at least 75% sure it found a person.
- **Cancelled jobs leave nothing behind.** A cancelled swap leaves no masks or anchor. A song cancelled at its last stage leaves no take.
- **The Director** says why the QA gate failed a take. A run with nothing to cut still ends with its counts. Cast and place stills use a picture model this machine has (FLUX3-K on a Spark without Qwen). A brain's "None" or "N/A" never reaches a prompt.
- **YuE2 memory refusals** give figures to a tenth of a GB and, on a card, name the card. A failed song frees its cache.
- **Credits:** tiktoken, the Qwen team's `qwen.tiktoken` and Openjutsu are credited. No machine paths or job owners remain in the recipe receipts.

## Tested

| Machine | What ran |
|---|---|
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Full suite: 1111 passed. studio-check api 12/12. YuE2 then MiniMax Music 3 songs. Character Swap at 480p in 335 s. Refusals for empty and gradient frames. Swap cancel. Director with the Bolt brain, 2 of 2 passed and cut. `--upgrade` 4.1.0 → 4.1.1. |
| Mac Studio (M5 Ultra) | Unit tests, picture, native 480p clip, song, export, QA gate, Bolt brain, Slate, Director. YuE2 and Swap say there is no Mac build. |
| RTX Pro 6000 96 GB (simulated: CUDA MPS 96G cap + `STUDIO_VRAM_GB=96` on a Spark) | Swap at 480p peaks at 49.4 GB. YuE2 on the PyTorch route. The largest clip followed by a song, with no OOM. Installer hints checked. |
| RTX 5090 32 GB (simulated: MPS 32G cap + fake nvidia-smi) | Video is refused by default and installs with `STUDIO_ALLOW_SMALL_VRAM=1`. The 64 GB RAM gate holds. Swap is refused without `STUDIO_ROOM_MB`, and with `STUDIO_ROOM_MB=84000` it completes (card peak 32.1 GB). YuE2: 120 s admitted, 300 s refused, and 300 s admitted with `STUDIO_ROOM_MB`. |

**Not verified on real x86 RTX cards.** The RTX numbers come from a GB10 capped with CUDA MPS. On those cards the engines build from source (`TF_SM=120`), and YuE2 uses PyTorch unless `YUE2_ANY_GPU=1`.

Character Swap peak memory, 5 s, int8 Ref2VA:

| | 480p | 768p |
|---|---|---|
| DGX Spark (machine) | 55.4 GB | 60.6 GB |
| 96 GB card | 49.4 GB | 52.7 GB |
| 32 GB card + `STUDIO_ROOM_MB` (machine) | 37.8 GB | 39.5 GB |

Thanks to Sam Wasserman for 3.4.0 and 4.1.0, and to spenchey for the per-machine labels and status in the Sparks room (#166).

body.name: 3.3.3: the DGX Spark's Bolt engine on TensorFold 1.1.5
body.body:
The DGX Spark's brain engine, **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt**, moves from Mia's 1.0.12 recipe (6f61d772 on TensorFold
46a08c18) to the same recipe at 89e1c8a (with ChriZzn's speed work) rebased onto **TensorFold 1.1.5**, drowzeys/TensorFold
branch `bolt-lilicorr-115`. NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter still runs inside it, and structured output (`libtfgrammar`),
pictures and video (`libtfvideo`) are in the build. Two changes over the recipe, neither touching the arithmetic: the
first token goes out before the drafter's first proposal, and a chat turn's last prompt-cache mark is kept at the
prompt's end, so a turn's new rows run in one pass instead of two.

Measured on a DGX Spark (GB10) with the Studio's own settings (4 streams, 65,536 tokens, 2 GiB of prompt cache,
pictures on), the same weights, one engine at a time, through a throwaway Studio (`/api/bolt/load`), greedy:

| | 3.3.2 engine (1.0.12) | 3.3.3 engine (1.1.5) |
|---|---|---|
| chat, 120 tokens | 57.0 tok/s, first token 128 ms | **65.8 tok/s**, 77 ms |
| 600-token plan | 67.6 tok/s, 156 ms | **76.1 tok/s**, 106 ms |
| edit (rewrite a paragraph) | 117.6 tok/s, 209 ms | **137.5 tok/s**, 143 ms |
| four plans at once | 140 tok/s | **204 tok/s** |
| held while loaded | 28.1 GB | 30.7 GB |

Both pass the same checks: a Slate plan through `/api/slate/brain` (JSON, four shots), tool calls (offered, forced and
named), `response_format` json_object and json_schema (the grammar holds; greedy, Bolt can run a schema's integer to
the token limit on both engines), a picture and a short video, an edit.

`spark/build-bolt.sh` now takes the engine from this release's archive (`bolt-cuda-ecdc7892-linux-aarch64.tar.gz`, sha256
pinned), then the carrier, then a build from source (nvcc, Zig 0.17.0, FFmpeg, libjpeg-turbo, xgrammar; about 15
minutes), and keeps the engine it replaces in `$PREFIX/bolt.previous` (move it back to `bolt` to roll back). Update a
Spark with `git pull && bash oneshot-setup.sh --upgrade`, then restart the app. The Mac keeps its Metal Bolt engine.

body.name: 3.3.0: the DGX Spark's music engine on TensorFold 1.1.5
body.body:
3.3.0 moves the studio's engines onto TensorFold 1.1.5 where that is a safe, measured step. Everything else stays where it was, and the README's "New in 3.3.0" says why, with the figures.

**DGX Spark: Music runs on TensorFold 1.1.5.** The music3 family (`music3-cuda-115`, 5505dbfa) is the same code on the 1.1.5 runtime. On one GB10, for a 30 s song:
- The song is byte for byte the same.
- It takes the same time to make, with the same 16.46 GB peak.
- The engine is ready 2.6x sooner: 12.5 to 16.2 s, against 32.6 to 69.8 s.

**Kept, after side-by-side runs on a GB10 with the same weights:**
- **Bolt on CUDA** (MiaAI-Lab's recipe): 56 to 153 tokens/s, against 36 to 115 for stock 1.1.5.
- **Drama 3 on CUDA** (the studio's engine): 33.9 frames/s, against a 0.77 real-time factor at best for stock 1.1.5.
- **The native FastH3 int8 engine:** 1.1.5's H3 is a bf16 rewrite, so moving ours over would be a port, not a rebase.
- **The Mac's MLX engines:** 1.1.5 has no Python or MLX package.

The Mac's engines are unchanged in this release.

**Update from 3.2.** Run `git pull && bash oneshot-setup.sh --upgrade` on a DGX Spark, then restart the app. It takes the new music engine from the carrier, with the checksums verified, and downloads no weights. Nothing changes for a Mac's engines.

**DGX Spark.** The carrier `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:3.3.0` (sha256:eb76d464…) holds the prebuilt CUDA engines for GB10:
- H3 (1f7ecc75)
- MiniMax Music 3 (5505dbfa, on TensorFold 1.1.5)
- Fish Audio Drama 3 (81173e6c)
- NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt (Mia's recipe 6f61d772)

**Mac (Apple silicon).** The installers download the assets below and check them by SHA-256. These are the 3.2.0 builds.
- `zig-engine-b19753ab-macos-arm64.tar.gz`: the native Zig + Metal FastH3 engine. sha256 775e9163…
- `bolt-metal-b4edaea5-macos-arm64.tar.gz`: the Metal engine for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt. sha256 58203b65…

No model weights are in the carrier or these assets.

Credit: Keys (drowzeys) and Sam Wasserman / Wasserman Productions. TensorFold 1.1.5 is by Ash Hart and the TensorFold contributors. Every model, engine and library is credited in CREDITS.md.

body.name: 3.2.0: the film studio, start to finish
body.body:
3.2.0 is the studio's code. Its engines are the 3.1.0 builds, so an update from 3.1 downloads no weights and no engines. A one-shot install works on either machine, and neither machine needs the other.

**What's new.** The full list is under "New in 3.2.0" in the README. In short:
- **Creative Engines in film order:** Video, Image, Sound, Story, Cast & Places, Director, Previs, Motion graphics, Edit and Night shift.
- **The Director:** from a logline to a checked cut.
- **The night shift:** plan a batch before bed and wake up to a reel and a notification on your phone.
- **A rough cut on the beat**, straight to DaVinci Resolve.
- **Motion graphics** with HyperFrames.
- **Finish:** the final cut and mix through Tesseract, to Resolve, Premiere or After Effects.
- **Restyle, Extend and Fix** on any clip in the Library.
- **Train your own LoRA** (DGX Spark).
- **Captions and search** in the Library.
- **Previs and prompts into a film**, from the filmmaker suite.
- **An install checklist** that asks what to install.

body.name: 2.9.2: Music on TensorFold's Metal engine, tutorial for every feature
body.body:
- **Mac: Music runs on TensorFold's native Metal engine.** On an M5 or later the Music tab now runs MiniMax Music 3
  on `music3-generate` built for Metal (Zig and Metal, no Python or MLX; TensorFold pull request #987, commit
  8c9559da), when `oneshot-setup.sh --music` has built it (`scripts/build-music3-metal.sh`). On the Mac Studio M5
  Ultra, against the MLX port int8, 60 s hip-hop, seed 7, three runs each: the autoregressive model 69 frames/s
  against 65, the whole song 59.5 to 63.0 s against 62.3 to 63.9 s, peak 17.8 GB against 28.1 GB. Through the app a
  song the model ended at 33.4 s took 35.2 s, load included, at 16.1 GB. Limits: it does not stream yet, so *Play
  while it's made* is MLX-only (`MUSIC3_BACKEND=mlx`); an M1 to M4 keeps the MLX port; measured on an M5 Ultra only.
  See [Music](https://github.com/drowzeys/keys-Wasserman-Slate-AI-Studio-powered-by-TensorFold-built-with-integrated-Fish-Audio-Drama3#music-minimax-music-3).

- **Tutorial and README brought up to date.** The Tutorial tab has new lessons for Voice (Fish Audio Drama 3), Music
  (MiniMax-Music3, including the Metal route), the Sparks tab, Sharp Spec, memory on a DGX Spark and the Library's
  actions, and stale lessons are corrected. TUTORIAL.md covers every feature through 2.9.2. The README's version
  notes now run newest first.
- **Carrier image unchanged:** `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:2.9.1` (nothing in it changed; the Metal
  Music engine is built from source on the Mac).

## Upgrade

On a Mac, in the clone:

```bash
git pull
bash oneshot-setup.sh --upgrade --music
```

On an M5 or later `--music` builds the Metal engine (Xcode's Metal toolchain needed; a few minutes) beside the MLX
port; on an M1 to M4 it keeps the MLX port. On a DGX Spark, `git pull` and restart the app: nothing to install.

Three changes to Music (MiniMax-Music3), one for each machine and one for the Mac's player. Every figure is one run
unless it says otherwise.

- **Mac: int8 weights by default.** The Studio starts the MLX engine (`music3-mlx`, now pinned at 6844b413) with
  `--quant int8`: the autoregressive model, its code-0 head and the depth decoder at 8 bits. On the Mac Studio M5
  Ultra the autoregressive model went from 40 to 65 frames a second and the peak from 27.6 to 20.5 GB; a 60 s song
  took about 63 s through the app (75.8 s in 2.9.0). Against ComfyUI's reference the code-0 logits keep cosine
  0.99994 (bf16 0.99997), 98.0 % greedy agreement, and Whisper's lyric scores over six same-seed songs stayed within
  their noise. `MUSIC3_QUANT=none` runs the bf16 weights. Limits: measured on an M5 Ultra only; other
  M-series chips are not measured.
- **Mac: play while it's made.** With the box ticked (the default where the engine streams) the song plays in the tab
  while it is made, from `GET /api/music/takes/{id}/live`, one stereo 44.1 kHz WAV. The sound is held back until
  playing will not run dry (the engine's measured no-stall start plus 3 s). Through the app, 60 s songs: first sound
  at about 7 s (7.6 and 6.4 s), playing from about 13 s (13.4 s both), no stall (the least buffer 4.0 s), made in
  63.4 and 61.0 s; a 30 s song played from 8.1 s. The kept take is the engine's finished WAV, the same samples that
  were played. Limits: a Mac only (no route on a Spark streams); only 30 s and 60 s were measured through the app, and
  the wait grows with the length (about 56 s for a 300 s song, from the engine's own figure); nobody has listened for
  seams. Details in [Music](https://github.com/drowzeys/keys-Wasserman-Slate-AI-Studio-powered-by-TensorFold-built-with-integrated-Fish-Audio-Drama3#music-minimax-music-3).
- **Music on a DGX Spark: TensorFold's CUDA engine for MiniMax Music 3 (MiniMax-Music3).** The Music tab on a Spark now
  runs `music3-generate`, TensorFold's native CUDA port (branch `music3-cuda`, 6b714531: Zig + CUDA, no Python at run
  time), wherever it is built and the weights are there; otherwise it falls back to ComfyUI's nodes as in 2.9.0.
  `MUSIC3_BACKEND=cuda|comfy` chooses; the tab's state says which route runs and, after a fall-back, why.
  - **int8 weights by default**, made on the GPU as the engine loads (no cache file): the autoregressive model, its
    head and the depth decoder at 8 bits. `MUSIC3_WEIGHTS=bf16` runs the checkpoint's own weights. It reads
    Comfy-Org's three files as they are (`~/spark-studio-models/MiniMax-Music3-Comfy`, `MUSIC3_MODEL` names another).
  - **Same lifecycle as the Mac engine:** a persistent server, loaded on the first song, holding
    `~/studio-gpu.lock.d` while loaded, unloaded after five idle minutes and before any other job, under the
    memory kill-guard; a studio ComfyUI that holds models is stopped before it loads. Never beside H3, Drama 3 or
    ComfyUI's models.
  - **Installed by** `bash oneshot-setup-spark.sh --music` (and `--upgrade` where the weights are): `spark/build-music3.sh`
    takes the prebuilt binary from the carrier image, or builds it with nvcc 12.9+ and Zig 0.17 (50 s on a GB10).
  - **Measured on one GB10** (int8, hip-hop lyrics, seed 7, 30 steps; one run each; memory is MemTotal - MemAvailable
    above the idle machine):

    | Song | TensorFold CUDA (int8) | ComfyUI's nodes (2.9.0) |
    |---|---|---|
    | 30 s, engine | 60.3 s | 131.0 s |
    | 60 s, engine | **123.9 s** (AR 73.9 s at 20.4 frames/s, DiT 46.4 s, DAV 3.6 s) | 260.6 s |
    | 120 s, engine | 252.0 s | 527.6 s |
    | 60 s through the app | **149.2 s** for the song (load 37.3 s, AR 68.2 s, DiT 40.4 s, DAV 3.3 s; the model ended it at 55.2 s), 171.4 s with Whisper's check (97 %, 164 of 169 words) | 270.6 s for the song (ComfyUI started for it; AR 166.5 s, DiT 94.3 s, DAV 4.0 s; 59.99 s made), 297.0 s with Whisper (96 %, 162 of 169), 29.4 GB at the peak: the same run of the 2.9.1 app with `MUSIC3_BACKEND=comfy` |
    | Peak memory, 60 s | 17.9 GB (18.7 GB through the app) | 29.3 GB |

    bf16 weights: a 60 s song in 194.3 s and 25.5 GB. Parity against ComfyUI's nodes and Whisper's lyric count
    passed on the engine branch (docs/recipes/minimax-music3-cuda.md there).
  - **Honest limits.** No streaming on the Spark: a song is heard when it is done. Built and measured on a GB10
    only (the build refuses another GPU unless `MUSIC3_ANY_GPU=1`; elsewhere use `MUSIC3_BACKEND=comfy`). Loading
    takes about 37 s each time the engine starts (int8 is made at load), so the first song after five idle minutes
    pays it again. Songs over 120 s are not measured on this engine; the memory estimate goes on at the measured slope.
- **Carrier image** `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:2.9.1` adds the prebuilt Spark `music3-generate`
  (`spark-music3/`) beside the H3 engine.

## Upgrade

On a Mac or a DGX Spark, in the clone:

```bash
git pull
bash oneshot-setup.sh --upgrade --music
```

`--music` installs the Music engine for that machine (the MLX port at 6844b413 on a Mac; on a Spark `music3-generate` from the carrier image `ghcr.io/drowzeys/keys-tensorfold-studio:2.9.1`) and the 22 GB of weights where they are missing. Leave `--music` out to upgrade without Music. Then restart the app.

| What | 2.7.0 (ComfyUI's bf16 blocks) | 2.7.1 (int8 engine) |
|---|---|---|

| 864x480, 124 frames | 140 s, 75.9 GB | 114 s (+12.5 s merge the first time), 57.6 GB |
| 1376x768, 124 / 192 / 243 frames | refused | 62.3 / 66.5 / 69.7 GB |

- The engine's clip and ComfyUI's bfloat16 clip show the same shot: pixel correlation 0.80, sound 0.89.

body.name: keys-TensorFold Studio 2.3 (Mac+DGXSpark): TensorFold's CUDA engine on the Spark, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo
body.body:
**Thank you to Ash Hart for TensorFold, FastVideo / Hao AI Lab for FastH3, MiniMax for H3, the Qwen team for Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, and the ComfyUI team for the runtime the DGX Spark build stands on.**

## What is new in 2.3

**The Studio now runs on an NVIDIA DGX Spark, on TensorFold's own CUDA engine.** FastH3's 50 transformer blocks run on a new CUDA family of TensorFold: the Mac engine's design in int8 on the GB10's tensor cores, written in Zig over the CUDA driver. ComfyUI, pinned, hosts the text encoder, the sampler and the decoders.

Measured on one DGX Spark, 124 frames (5 s), 8 passes, text to video, models loaded, one run each:

| Size | TensorFold engine (int8) | ComfyUI's own blocks (bf16) |
|---|---|---|
| 864x480 | **73 s** (a pass 7.1 s) | 118 to 121 s (a pass 10.5 s) |
| 1280x720 | **183 s** (a pass 18 s) | not measured |
| 1344x768 | **about 195 s** (a pass 20.5 s) | 289 s (a pass 29.4 s) |

- Why int8: the GB10's tensor cores run int8 products at 245 TOPS and bf16 ones at 122. The engine's own matrix kernel reaches 150 to 175 on FastH3's shapes; PyTorch's stock int8 routine about 52.
- Against ComfyUI's bf16 blocks on the same input with dense attention, the stream after all 50 blocks has cosine 0.998. A repeat of a seed gives a bit-identical clip.
- The video decode uses ComfyUI's 8-bit decoder: 14 s for 124 frames of 864x480 against 26 s, the same picture to 42 to 44 dB.
- Longer clips: 10 s at 1280x720 took 444 s (378 s on an M5 Ultra for the same prompt); a 30 s chained clip at 864x480 took 611 s.
- The transformer is held in int8, 21 GB instead of 42. The first use converts the checkpoint (about 90 s) and saves the int8 copy beside it; later starts read it in seconds.

**Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo makes the images, on both machines.** The Qwen team's own 8-step checkpoint replaces the base model with Viggle's adapter. On an M5 Ultra a 1344x768 image takes 8.9 s (9.4 s before) and peaks at 15 GiB instead of 28. On the Spark it takes 9.5 s with the model loaded. An earlier Mac install keeps working on what it has; the setup fetches Turbo's transformer (14 GB) and links the rest.

**One install command.** `bash oneshot-setup.sh` picks the Mac or the Spark build by itself. The web app's header says which one you are in: a purple `MAC · APPLE SILICON MX · H3-METAL` or a green `DGX SPARK · NVIDIA GB10 · H3-CUDA`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/drowzeys/keys-TensorFold-Studio-Mac-DGXSpark-64GB-VRam-Min.git && cd keys-TensorFold-Studio-Mac-DGXSpark-64GB-VRam-Min
bash oneshot-setup.sh
bash scripts/app.sh              # http://127.0.0.1:7870
```

## Two things we learned about prompts

- **For people at 864x480, start from an image** (prompt, still, then video: the app's default flow). Text straight to video at that size gave distorted close-up faces, on ComfyUI's blocks and on the engine alike; from a still the face holds.
- **A shot with several linked actions works better as one action per segment**, each opening on the last frame of the one before (the Production tab), than as one prompt.

## Unchanged, and not tested

- Video on the Mac is unchanged, and so is its speed (5.3 s a pass at 864x480).
- The Spark build has FastH3 only: no MiniMax H3 Turbo and no 2x decoder. A pass is about 1.35x an M5 Ultra's at 864x480.
- Not tested: a download of the Spark's models from nothing (they were already on the test machine), any GPU other than the GB10, two Sparks on one clip, clips longer than 15 s in one piece on the Spark, and any Mac other than the M5 Ultra.
- Engine source: [drowzeys/TensorFold `h3-1.0.4`](https://github.com/drowzeys/TensorFold/tree/h3-1.0.4), one commit for both the Mac's Metal engine and the Spark's CUDA engine, on the TensorFold 1.0.4 base (a fork; upstream is [ashhart/TensorFold](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold)). Moving from the 1.0.2 base changed no output and no timing: on each machine the same seed gives a bit-identical clip.
